record.original_question: Let a bounded operator T on a complex Hilbert space be complex symmetric if T = C T* C for some conjugation C. In finite dimensions, every complex symmetric operator is known to be unitarily equivalent to a direct sum of irreducible complex symmetric matrices and matrices formed as the direct sum of A and A^t, where A is irreducible and is not itself complex symmetric, and irreducible means not unitarily equivalent to a nontrivial direct sum. What is the corresponding infinite-dimensional analogue of this finite-dimensional decomposition theorem for complex symmetric operators?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let H be a separable complex Hilbert space and let B(H) denote the algebra of bounded linear operators on H. A conjugation on H is an antilinear map C : H → H that is involutive (C² = I) and isometric (⟨Cx, Cy⟩ = ⟨y, x⟩ for all x, y ∈ H). A bounded operator T ∈ B(H) is called complex symmetric if there exists a conjugation C on H such that T = C T* C. An operator A ∈ B(H) is called irreducible if it is not unitarily equivalent to a nontrivial orthogonal direct sum B ⊕ D of two bounded operators on nonzero Hilbert spaces.

In the finite-dimensional case (dim H < ∞), every complex symmetric operator T is unitarily equivalent to an orthogonal direct sum of blocks of two types:
 (i) irreducible complex symmetric matrices, and
 (ii) blocks of the form A ⊕ A^t, where A is an irreducible matrix that is not itself complex symmetric and A^t denotes its transpose with respect to some orthonormal basis.

Problem: Formulate and prove the analogous structural decomposition theorem for complex symmetric operators on an infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space. That is, determine whether every complex symmetric operator T ∈ B(H) admits a canonical decomposition (in some appropriate sense, e.g., as a direct sum or direct integral) into "irreducible" complex symmetric pieces together with pieces of the form A ⊕ CA*C where A is irreducible and not complex symmetric, and identify the precise formulation under which such a decomposition holds.
artifact.status_search_result: The infinite-dimensional analogue of the finite-dimensional decomposition theorem for complex symmetric operators is regarded as an open structural problem. Subsequent work (e.g., Liu's 2019 paper on reducible and irreducible approximation of complex symmetric operators in J. London Math. Soc.) addresses related approximation questions but does not produce a full canonical decomposition theorem analogous to the finite-dimensional one. No source verifying a complete solution was found.

status_evidence.title: Reducible and irreducible approximation of complex symmetric operators
status_evidence.snippet: Studies reducible and irreducible approximation in the set of all complex symmetric operators on a separable, complex Hilbert space H of infinite dimension.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work investigates the structure of complex symmetric operators in infinite dimensions via approximation, but does not give a complete analogue of the finite-dimensional decomposition.

status_evidence.title: Mathematical and physical aspects of complex symmetric operators
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of the theory of complex symmetric operators including their structural properties.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys of the field discuss the finite-dimensional decomposition and indicate that the infinite-dimensional structure problem remains structurally open.
